idiom_name: single dispatch-loop guard + verifier callback table
implementation_notes: C has no request pipeline in the standard library, so the enforcement point is hand-written: one guard function that the server's dispatch loop calls before it invokes a route handler, with verification behind a table of function pointers (int (*verify)(const char *cred, struct principal *out)) so user stores or token validators can be swapped without touching the guard. The guard owns policy and challenge only; credential extraction (parsing the Authorization header or session id) and constant-time comparison (CRYPTO_memcmp) belong to the mechanism. The full structure is justified when several front ends share one credential policy; a single-purpose daemon is better served by an inline check.
pitfalls: Comparing credentials or tokens with strcmp/strncmp leaks timing information; the delegated verifier must use a constant-time comparison such as CRYPTO_memcmp.
The principal must live in the per-connection request struct; a static or global buffer is shared across connections in threaded servers.
Parsing the Authorization header in the guard and again inside the mechanism guarantees the two parsers drift; extraction belongs to exactly one place.
